name: stack-agents
description: Run parallel AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, opencode) across git worktrees, each in its own tmux session, from one sidebar.

commands.title: Stack: Focus Next Worktree Needing Attention
Stack: Open Session to the Side
Stack: Attach Latest Screenshot to Agent

stack.worktreesDirectory.description: Directory where worktrees are created (relative to the workspace root) Can be set for everyone who clones the repo in .stack/config.json; a value set here wins.

stack.defaultBaseBranch.description: Branch new worktrees start from, preselected in the New Task form. When this branch does not exist, Stack uses the repository's own main line (the first of main/master/develop it finds, locally or on a remote), and only then the current branch. Can be set for everyone who clones the repo in .stack/config.json; a value set here wins.

stack.setupScript.description: Script to run after creating a worktree Can be set for everyone who clones the repo in .stack/config.json; a value set here wins.

stack.setupInTerminal.description: Run the setup script in a visible terminal you can type into, and start the agent without waiting for it — for setup scripts that ask questions. Off (default): it runs in the background, its output in the Stack output channel, and the agent starts once it has finished. Can be set for everyone who clones the repo in .stack/config.json; a value set here wins.

stack.teardownScript.description: Script to run before deleting a worktree Can be set for everyone who clones the repo in .stack/config.json; a value set here wins.

stack.promptPrefix.description: Text prepended to the first prompt of every agent you launch (new tasks, the control session, waking an idle one) — sent on its own when there is no prompt otherwise. A personal setting, not meant for .stack/config.json: put reminders here that a fresh agent would not otherwise pick up, e.g. which skill to check first.

stack.defaultProvider.description: Primary agent: the one the big launch button on each worktree card starts. The chevron next to it opens the rest.

enumDescriptions: Aside: monochrome with a single lime accent, a composer, filter chips, worktrees grouped by state and a health strip.
Claude: warm terracotta accent, a prompt composer at the top and worktrees grouped by what they need from you. Follows the VS Code theme.
Mission control: state counters that filter, an attention queue and cards with a metadata grid. Follows the VS Code theme.
stack.sidebarStyle.description: How the Stack sidebar looks. Switches live, without a reload. The same worktrees and actions are in every style; only the layout and colours differ. Also under "Stack: Switch Sidebar Style".

stack.notifyOnAttention.description: Show a native OS notification, with a chime on macOS, when an agent finishes or asks for permission while VS Code is in the background. Off means no notification and no sound. The sidebar attention badge is always shown regardless.

stack.focusMode.description: Clean-slate switching: when you switch worktree, close the other worktrees' editor tabs and agent terminals so only the active one is on screen. Off (default) makes switching an instant reveal with no flicker.

enumDescriptions: Every session (agent or shell) gets its own terminal tab, so several can be open at once: drag them into editor groups side by side and resize them like any editor.
One terminal per worktree; picking a session switches what that terminal shows (tmux windows, with tmux's status bar).
stack.sessionTabs.description: How a worktree's sessions open in the editor: a tab per session, or one terminal per worktree. Applies to terminals opened after the change.

stack.scopeSearchToActiveWorktree.description: Hide non-active worktree folders from text search and Quick Open (writes search.exclude to each worktree's .vscode/settings.json)

composeFile.description: Base compose file (relative to each worktree)

overrideFile.description: Worktree-only override layered on top of composeFile; use ${HTTP_PORT} etc. for the auto-generated ports. Compose appends its `ports` to the compose file's instead of replacing them, so a port hard-coded there is published by every worktree: use a variable there, or `ports: !override` here.

ports.description: Env var names to auto-generate a per-worktree port for (e.g. HTTP_PORT). Configuring at least one enables the Docker start/stop button. DEBUG_PORT reuses the worktree's debug port.

basePort.description: First port of the docker range

portStride.description: Size of the port block each worktree owns

stack.docker.description: Per-worktree docker orchestration: compose files and auto-generated ports Can be set for everyone who clones the repo in .stack/config.json; a value set here wins.

stack.debugBasePort.description: Base port for the debugger. Each worktree gets base+N Can be set for everyone who clones the repo in .stack/config.json; a value set here wins.

stack.debugTemplate.description: launch.json template for each worktree. Use {{PORT}} and {{WORKTREE_PATH}} as placeholders Can be set for everyone who clones the repo in .stack/config.json; a value set here wins.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with Stack
walkthroughs.description: Several AI agents in parallel, one git worktree each, and a sidebar that tells you who needs you.

steps.title: Make sure tmux is there
steps.description:
Agents run inside tmux so they survive window reloads. If it is missing, the Stack view offers to install it.
[Open Stack](command:workbench.view.extension.stack-container)

steps.title: Create a worktree and launch an agent
steps.description:
One task, one branch, one worktree, one agent. Describe the task; Stack cuts the branch, creates the worktree and starts the agent in it.
[New task](command:stack.newTask)

steps.title: Switch between worktrees
steps.description:
Cmd+Shift+] and Cmd+Shift+[ (Ctrl on Linux) jump between worktrees. Search, Quick Open and breakpoints follow you.
[Next worktree](command:stack.focusNextWorktree)

steps.title: Review the diff and talk back
steps.description: Each card has a diff button: comment on lines and send them straight to the agent. Drop a screenshot onto the agent's terminal to attach it, or press Cmd+Alt+V there to attach the latest one from your screenshots folder.

steps.title: Set up Docker, debugging and scripts
steps.description:
The gear in the Worktrees header opens settings: a Docker stack per worktree, a debugger port per worktree, setup and teardown scripts. Stack prefills what it finds in the repo.
[Open settings](command:stack.openSettings)

steps.title: Share the setup with your team
steps.description:
Project settings save to .stack/config.json. Commit it and everyone who clones the repo gets the same worktrees, ports and scripts.
[Open settings](command:stack.openSettings)

scripts.preversion: npm run typecheck && npm run test:coverage
